overallNotes: Hannah Louise Mercer (b. 1988) is a mid-career registrar at the Providence Museum of Art whose ~3.5-year arc (Jan 2025 - Jun 2028) traces a remarkable transformation from competent-but-anxious individual contributor into the museum's lead registrar — the architect of a rebuilt collections and loan-cycle system. Key arc: (1) Onboarding reveals an ISTJ personality, Museum Studies background, and deep commitment to collections integrity. (2) A photography loan request exposes widespread location and records unreliability, launching a phased collections integrity review. (3) The cleanup pilot confirms systemic problems — objects where database, tag, and label all disagree — forcing movement controls. (4) A catastrophic crate incident (partial repair overruled her full-rebuild recommendation, then failed in transit) triggers insurer scrutiny and becomes the crucible that gives her leverage for policy change. (5) Post-crate: she converts the failure into mandatory outgoing loan controls, incident packets, and eventually quarterly spot audits and a cross-department checklist. (6) Parallel personal life: meets Alex Chen (library preservation technician) in Jul 2025, evolves to steady partnership by Aug 2026; Priya (roommate since grad school) moves to Boston in 2027 prompting a solo apartment; develops used-mystery-paperback habit and task-specific music strategies. (7) Culmination: a multi-lender exhibition completes full cycle without documentation scramble, verified records hit near-target, overdue catalog drops below danger zone, and she presents a board-facing summary. Pattern: Hannah's strength is translating anxiety into systems — she reacts to every stressor by building structure (tension logs, readiness checklists, incident packets, freezer meal plans, approved-vs-audit decision trees). Recurring theme: institutions prefer cheap short-term fixes over prevention; her arc is learning to make long-term prevention politically undeniable. Data issues: emotional_tone field always reads 'neutral' despite clear emotional variance (crate disaster = negative, Melville date = positive); tags are overly broad ('work', 'health', 'finance') and never capture specificity; decisions field is occasionally truncated mid-sentence; focus and summary fields are quote fragments rather than distilled descriptions. The agent sometimes confuses Priya (roommate) with Marta (mentor) or refers to Priya as 'sister' incorrectly.
